content:
- When sentiment is positive (1.0) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- When sentiment is negative (-1.0), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean or spike magnitude.
- Model consistently over-estimates early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) after a spike; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 7 days.
- Model under-estimates late in horizon (last 5–7 days) after a spike; apply upward bias of 0.5–1.5% for last 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for each alternating cycle.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and model is over-forecasting, apply 1–2% downward correction to avoid over-leverage.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses the “peak” of sentiment-driven rallies; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast at 15–20 day mark if sentiment turns positive.
